title: How Corbyn Besson got Tzuyu from TWICE on his hit song "Blink" 👀 📈
text:
Hi coconuts! Today’s episode of “Middle Row w Coco Mocoe” features an artist that I believe should be on your radar.
Corbyn Besson was formerly known for being a child star in the boyband “Why Don’t We” with hit songs like “8 letters”. Now, he is breaking solo. Ahead of his first EP, “Head First”, he released a song called “Blink” featuring Tzuyu from the K-Pop girl group TWICE.
He sat on this song for 8 months, waiting for the right moment and collaborator. And thank goodness he did because now the song has 13,000,000+ views on YouTube and 15,000,000+ listens on Spotify.
Corbyn Besson originally started out in the boy band “Why Don’t We”. They were a group of kids who met online and decided, “Why don’t we start a boy band?”. Hence the name.
After a whirlwind 4 years together, like playing in Madison Square Garden and collaborating with Logan Paul on videos that got 230+ million views on YouTube, it all came to a halt in 2020 with the pandemic. Fast forward to a legal battle with their former manager in 2022, where allegations of mental and financial abuse surfaced ( BBC ). In 2025, a judge ruled they could no longer use the name, “Why Don’t We”.
Corbyn Besson began working on his upcoming EP, Head First . He created a song called “Blink” where they felt strongly the chorus should be a female voice. They sat on the song for over 8 months while waiting for the right person.
His A&R set up a meeting between the two of them at Lollapalooza (right before both of them were to hit the stage with emotions at a high). After their meeting at Lolla, they were off to the races.
This episode of “Middle Row with Coco Mocoe” chronicles the story of how he created a song that now has 13,000,000+ views on YouTube — from being mobbed by fans while filming in Seoul, South Korea to the regrets he had with releasing other songs in the build up to this one.
